title: QuickTune console configurator — proto notes
content:
Purpose / one-liner:
QuickTune = in-console guided tuner that helps engineers pick a serving profile (latency target, cost cap, accuracy guardrails) and generates a safe config bundle (batching/quantization/prefetch/cache policy) plus a preview of expected cost/latency impact. Goal: make sensible production tradeoffs approachable without jumping into infra tickets or model ops docs.

Why:
- PMs/Engs keep asking for a fast way to reduce token-unit cost per-route without risking user-visible regressions.
- Ops teams can ship defaults but customers want quick experiments per route without waiting for SRE.
- A guided UI lowers bar for adopting Dedicated/Private optimization knobs.

Beneficiaries / personas:
- Product engineers: want to try cost-lowering tweaks and see immediate projected ROI.
- Platform engineers/SRE: want validated, reversible config bundles with safe rollouts.
- Solutions/SE: can prototype customer recommendations in-console and export to config.

Core flows (sketch):
1) Route selection: user picks an API route or model endpoint in Console
2) Snapshot baseline: QuickTune runs a short eval on recent telemetry (sample of requests) and shows baseline: median latency, p50/p95, token counts, unit cost per 1k tokens, output-similarity to baseline model (sim score).
3) Choose objective: slider or preset — e.g., "reduce cost by X%" or "meet latency ≤ Y ms" or "maximize quality (min drift)".
4) Preview proposals: UI shows 3 ranked proposals (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive). Each proposal lists: batching config (max_batch_size, batching_window_ms), quantization profile (int8, fp16, mixed), KV cache policy (prefix-only, full-session), warmup strategy (mini-warmup requests), expected delta in cost/latency, and a quality risk rating.
5) Simulate: run a quick dry-run (on sampled requests) to estimate generation differences. Diff view: token-level cost, output-SIM (ROUGE/embedding-sim), failure modes flagged (truncation, OOM risk).
6) Apply / schedule rollout: create a canary deployment (1% traffic) + auto rollback triggers (quality drop > X or latency > Y). Option to export bundle to Dedicated/Private config or open a ticket with SRE.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to reduce per-token cost for /search route by 30% while keeping summaries indistinguishable to users, so I can hit my cost targets for Q4.
- As an SRE, I want any QuickTune proposal to include preflight checks (GPU footprint, memory headroom) and an automatic rollback plan, so I don't get paged for regressions.
- As an SE doing an onsite pilot, I want to export QuickTune config as a zip/config repo snippet to apply in a Private deployment.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI flow to pick route and baseline computed from last 24h telemetry (p50/p95, avg tokens, failure rate).
- Generate 3 proposals with clear metric deltas and risk indicator.
- Dry-run simulation that compares outputs via embedding-sim and reports delta.
- Ability to create a canary rollout with rollback thresholds wired to existing rollout infra.
- Audit log entry for every applied bundle and exported config.

Metrics to validate success (OKRs):
- Time-to-config: < 10 minutes from route selection to applied canary (MVP target).
- Adoption: 15% of routes with >1000 requests/day try QuickTune within 3 months of launch.
- Cost impact: average 12–20% token-unit cost reduction for routes that accept proposals.
- Failure/reversion rate: < 5% rollbacks per applied bundle.

Console UI notes (very rough):
- Left panel: route selector + historical sparkline
- Center: baseline panel + objective selector + proposals card stack
- Right: simulation diff viewer (side-by-side original vs tuned output, similarity score and examples)
- CTA: "Apply canary" (opens modal with rollout knobs), "Export bundle"
- Inline help: show brief explanation of each knob and a tooltip on risk estimation methodology.

Backend pieces (ops):
- Telemetry sampler job (samples N recent requests per route, obfuscates PII)
- Offline estimator service: given sampled requests + model variant, runs simulated generation at scaled rate on low-cost infra (can use quantized runtime) and computes sim metrics + cost delta estimator.
- Proposal generator: rules + heuristic optimizer (greedy search over batched window, batch size, quant profile) with safety constraints: memory <= host headroom margin, latency target not exceeded in simulation p95.
- Config bundler + rollout integration with existing rollouts API.

Risk and unknowns (open questions):
- Data privacy: sampling needs redaction pipeline (PII, user data). Who owns approval? Legal/Privacy review needed.
- Simulation fidelity: simulated quantized run may not fully match production (different kernels). How to surface confidence? Need calibration dataset.
- Cost estimation accuracy: token pricing for hosted vs dedicated varies; need price model in estimator.
- Multi-tenant isolation: exports for Private must not leak telemetry from other customers.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (research, 2w): small prototype of estimator using 50k sampled inputs for 3 routes. Manual scoring by PM/SE.
- Phase 1 (MVP, 6w): UI route selection, baseline, 3 proposals, dry-run on sampled requests, create canary rollout API call.
- Phase 2 (hardening, 8w): export bundles for Private, rich simulation with GPU-backed estimator, audit and privacy gating.
- Phase 3 (scale): ML-based optimizer for proposal generation, A/B test experiments, in-console suggested defaults per vertical.

Quick engineering notes / shortcuts for prototype:
- Start with quantization choices = [fp16, int8]. Use our internal quant-runtime shim for quick runs.
- Use 24h telemetry but cap sample to 2000 examples to bound compute.
- For similarity compute use embedding-sim (sentence-transformer) precomputed in a cheap CPU cluster.
- Show estimated cost deltas with conservative margin (+10%) to avoid overpromising.

To-dos (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Sync with privacy (Hannah) about sampling & redaction. (assign in INF-872)
- [ ] Quick spike: run a hand-sample simulation for /summarize and /search. (owner: kai)
- [ ] Mockup minimal console screens (owner: tess) — low-fidelity first.
- [ ] Draft rollout guard thresholds and link to rollout service API.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep the UI language non-MLy: talk about "speed vs cost" and "quality guardrails" not "quantization" by default — advanced toggle for power users.
- Consider "suggested savings" email digest for PMs if QuickTune finds big wins overnight.

Slack threads / refs: #devx-cost-ux has past discussion, worth pulling 2024-07 thread with SRE objections to auto-quantizing.

Longer-term/ideas (parking lot):
- Offer "one-click optimizer" for new routes (auto-propose on creation).
- Integrate with Optimize: keep a catalog of per-customer safe profiles learned over time.
- Marketplace: prebuilt QuickTune presets for common workloads (summarization, retrieval, chat).

End of brain-dump. Will iterate after 1:1 with Kai and Tess.
